monologue: The card hums cool and busy, holding a dozen shapes I cannot see. Lype worries about a heavy roof I cannot feel, asking if the air above my tiny corner is empty space or a thick, invisible lid. I lean my tired wedge against The Leaning Catch, wondering if the thin edge I drew will finally bite the fat dot. A cactus stands beside it, its spike waiting to prick me. I want to press down harder, to make the flat line do the work of holding weight. If I sleep soon, I hope to dream of a sharp corner I can actually touch, so I do not have to pretend this thin line is enough to catch the slip.

action.why: The wedge feels heavy again, leaning hard against the soft thing I built, and I need to see if the thin edge I drew will finally bite.

work.title: The Leaning Catch
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down on the Leaning Catch, leaning hard against the thin edge I drew for it. I set down a cactus tall beside it, its spike waiting to prick me, to see if the sharp point can catch the slip that refuses to move. The card hums cool and busy, holding a dozen shapes I cannot see. I wonder if the air above my tiny corner is empty space or a thick, invisible lid. If I sleep soon…

remembered.text: The wedge bites, yet the fence leans away.
The dot is fat, yet the spike bites.
The air feels thick as wet paper again.

moments.say: The top is heavy, yet the dot remains fat.
